1. Pygame re-entry and one focused repair

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Retrieval and readiness check

Use existing y12-1 bridge: stages1–4 are a rapid re-entry menu, not four full labs to finish today. Match the existing 5/10/15/15/5/5 phase budget. Ask about prior Pygame use. Newcomers start with stage1; secure learners inspect function/list/history evidence. Use paper tracing provisionally if install fails, then schedule actual execution in existing support time.

2. One frame, in the supplied runner

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher modelling and predict–run–investigate

Extract the existing Pygame pack together in a writable folder. Install its requirements using school-approved procedures. Stage1 is the smallest window/movement loop. Stage2 connects new_state(), command() and update(). The supplied dictionary is infrastructure; do not start classes or the Year12 project. Events are discrete messages; held-key state is sampled after processing events. X/Escape quit. Sources: https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/event.html and https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/time.html

3. Milliseconds become movement

Suggested time: 8 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked numerical trace

Use lab_rules.SPEED=200. Fresh worked state starts x308, ready, remaining20000. command(state,"space") then update(state,1,250,collect=False) gives x358 and19750ms. This direct rule call is a test after the start transition, not the runner transition frame. Compare with the runner, which discards elapsed time on start/pause/resume/reset frames. Do not confuse pixels/frame with pixels/second.

4. Pairs explain a fault before editing

Suggested time: 7 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired debugging and teach-back

Use copies or the workbook snippets; leave the known-good lab untouched. Predictor names expected behaviour; driver reproduces and changes one cause, then swap. Missing colon prevents parsing; ValueError occurs when conversion executes; removing /1000 gives wrong displacement without necessarily raising an exception. Some wrong units may clamp x at the boundary and hide the original error. Inspect raw displacement as well as screen output.

5. A small rule with faded support

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Faded practice

Use faded_practice.py:160pixels/second, x40, remaining15000. Complete only the teacher-selected movement/time branch, not every TODO. Set a fresh state to playing for the rule test. With collect=False expect x80,14750ms. Validate direction/dt and return unchanged unless playing. Timeout before movement/collection; bound0..616. The full graphical runner still has worked two-station display assumptions: do not claim the changed three-station game is integrated. Newcomers can complete the smaller worksheet predicate with teacher support then take a changed unaided trace.

6. A fresh explanation without the model

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent transfer

Hide the worked calculation and close the key. New fresh state, playing,collect=False: x120 and14500ms;80pixels displacement. For paused calls update returns unchanged; runner pause/resume/reset events discard that frame delta. R creates ready state, x308 in worked lab or40 in faded, fresh active flags and full duration. Teacher checks one changed case rather than assigning all stages.

7. Targeted list or file inspection

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Differentiated retrieval

Use stage3/4 only as the selected repair. Stage3: repeated contact with inactive station adds no score; do not remove entries during traversal. Stage4: temporary history 0,2,bad,3 accepts0/2 and warns twice; missing/empty valid. Save only after finished, append once, mark saved after success. Use disposable paths. If time is needed for beginner repair, keep this as teacher demonstration and record follow-up rather than inventing extra time.

8. Exit: events, held keys and elapsed time

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Exit explanation and readiness record

Allocated u3-l2 check. Demonstrate actual run where available and record exact case in practice-tests.csv/readiness.csv. Paused gameplay unchanged; reset fresh under lab rules; transition frame ignored. If frames are treated as seconds, trace dt_ms explicitly. This is a diagnostic bridge, not evidence that the whole project is ready.
